title: Back to Milwaukee and Tommy Fox in Superior
summary: Rejecting the WPA band, he works six months in Duluth and Superior for Tommy Fox at thirty-five dollars a week; Fox's son drowns.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: You mean they never worked, the WPA band?

No, man... They worked... Every now and then they might get a gig, you know. But the money was no good, see, like maybe five or six dollars. And like, what can you do with that after you're gonna pay your rent and live?
So I got a job with a guy named Tommy Fox up there...
In Milwaukee. But this was to go up in Duluth... This was Superior.
Yeah, Duluth and Superior up there on the lake.
Yeah. Talkin' about cold, boy oh boy... I thought Minot was bad, but man, Duluth and Superior were somethin' else.

And I stayed up there for six months, bought me a new Martin trumpet. I thought I was doing something, plus I was making thirty-five dollars a week, every week, which was a godsend. I needed it, boy, because it sure was cold up there. I swear, man! Whew. So I'll never forget that.

And Tommy Fox, the bandleader, he lost his son up there on the lake, Lake Superior. He and his son and his daughter went out swimming. Anyway, the boy got drowned, because he didn't know how to swim that good. Which was a sad affair, because it was a band affair. Tommy was a beautiful cat, and we all loved him and everything, but we couldn't help it about his son, because he was a beautiful son.
